summary: Iter-12 security/audit testing: share-audit $inc, forensic clinic-mismatch log, and in-memory sliding-window rate-limit on /api/reports/shared/{token} (20/60s) + /api/queue/public/{clinic_id} (120/60s). All 27 new test cases + 28/28 iter11 regression pass. Total 55 green.
critical_code_review_comments: rate_limit.py is single-process-local (noted in the module docstring). If the backend ever scales to multiple Uvicorn workers, the per-IP budget becomes N× per-worker — swap for Redis. Fine for now.
_client_ip in rate_limit.py and reports.py are identical — candidate for a shared util to avoid drift.

When the preview is fronted by Cloudflare without a client-pinned X-Forwarded-For, the first XFF entry can rotate per request, which made my initial (non-XFF-pinned) rate-limit test flaky. This is a test-environment artifact — in production, the limiter will see a stable caller IP because the ingress sets XFF. Tests now pin XFF explicitly, which also validates the 'respects X-Forwarded-For from ingress' spec.
share-audit endpoint correctly projects out both `_id` and `token_hash`; verified in test assertions.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-12 security surface verified. Rate-limit tests require X-Forwarded-For to be explicitly pinned when running through the Cloudflare-fronted preview URL; otherwise CF may rotate the first XFF entry and the per-IP bucket never fills. Each rate-limit test calls _restart_backend() to flush the in-memory buckets before firing — keep that pattern. Forensic log test greps /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log for 'share_link.clinic_mismatch'. Rate-limiter runs BEFORE JWT decode, so forensic-log tests must run in a fresh 60s window. The share-audit response is verified to exclude both `_id` and `token_hash`.
